name: Apache crown dance (Mountain Spirit songs)
lineage: Apache crown dance (Gaan or Mountain Spirit dance) ceremonial-performance tradition of the Western Apache and broader Apachean (Mescalero, Jicarilla, Chiricahua, San Carlos, White Mountain) communities. Performance features four masked dancers representing the Gaan Mountain Spirits accompanied by song-leader-and-drummer plus chorus, with the Gaan dancers wearing tall slatted wooden crowns and yucca-fiber kilts. Performance contexts include the Sunrise Ceremony (the four-day female puberty rite, the most important Apache ceremony) and various social-and-healing occasions. Repertoire is restricted in non-Apache circulation; the public-demonstration crown-dance performances at the annual Apache fairs (San Carlos, White Mountain) constitute the principal external-cultural visibility.
